text:
Anya: Heads-up — after flipping on the dynamic-kernel-scheduler rollout (v2) in dedicated, our structured-output eval suite shows a 3.2% absolute drop in exact-match and a few examples where JSON keys are reordered/missing and some hallucinated fields. Repro steps + logs below.

Mike: ack, can you paste the failing example and the exact commit/flag? :eyes:

Anya: failing example (shortened):
```
Input: generate invoice JSON for order #123
Expected: {\"order_id\":123, \"items\":[...], \"total\": 42.75}
Output: {\"items\":[...], \"total\": 42.75, \"billing_address\": \"Unknown\", \"order_id\":123}
```
Flag: runtime.dynamic_kernel_scheduler = on (rolled 2023-11-09T22:14Z)
Commit: runtime/scheduler@f7a9b2d

Sandeep: interesting — ordering alone shouldn't matter for JSON EM unless the eval matcher is strict, but hallucinated billing_address is worrying. Any diffs in logits or token-level traces?

Anya: yes, token-level delta shows a short burst where next-token probs change around token index 18 (right after prefix). I attached profiler samples below.

Anya: kernel selection trace snippet (runtime debug):
```
[2023-11-09T22:14:03.112Z] request_id=abc kernel_select: seq_len=64 -> kernel=fp8_mixed_v2
[2023-11-09T22:14:03.120Z] request_id=abc batcher: merged with batch_id=42
[2023-11-09T22:14:03.146Z] kv_cache: attach -> backend=compressed_int4
[2023-11-09T22:14:03.170Z] kernel_switch: mid-sequence -> kernel=int8_lowlatency (reason=batch_size>1)
[2023-11-09T22:14:03.171Z] kv_cache: migrate-layout -> partial-reshard
```
Two things jump out: mid-sequence kernel switches + KV cache migration in-flight.

Jess: that sequence is messy — we haven't fully proven correctness for on-the-fly KV layout migration when kernels change precision. Could be a rounding/pack/unpack ordering bug.

Mike: I can repro locally with the small harness. Running with dynamic-kernel-scheduler on vs pinned-fp32: I see the same hallucinated field in ~1.6% of runs on our eval set. If I set runtime.force_kernel=fp32 it's gone.

Sandeep: do we have perf traces comparing token latencies across the switch? Might be padding/batching heuristics causing a different prefix sent to model.

Anya: profiler flame snippet (token timeline, simplified):
```
TokenIdx: 0..17 => kernel=fp8_mixed_v2  avg_latency=5.2ms
TokenIdx: 18 => kernel_switch event  avg_latency spike=18ms
TokenIdx: 19.. => kernel=int8_lowlatency avg_latency=4.8ms
KV ops: pack/unpack at switch (+3ms)
```

Anya: Also saw a rare log: "kv_cache: gap-detected during partial-reshard" — looks like we may be missing a fence or we apply updates in different order depending on kernel.

Jess: hypothesis: packing format differs between fp8_mixed_v2 and int8_lowlatency; if migration code assumes symmetric layout we might reorder KV entries. That would change subsequent generation probability.

Mike: confirmed packing format mismatch in codegen: fp8 path uses 2-byte headers per-block, int8 uses 1-byte header + offset table. Migration tries to translate but relies on per-shard ordering which fails on small-batch merges.

Sandeep: ok plan: 1) roll back dynamic-kernel-scheduler rollout to unaffected hosts (canary rollback) 2) add assertion in kv migration about total-key-count and checksum 3) add unit test that simulates mid-sequence kernel flip + concurrent batch merge 4) add telemetry to log kernel_switch + kv_checksum per request_id.

CanaryBot: deploy rollback started for runtime/scheduler group canary. 4 hosts targeted.

Anya: quick mitigation already applied: we set runtime.dynamic_kernel_scheduler=false on the canary pool at 22:25Z — subsequent runs look clean. Will schedule full rollback if we see more fails.

Jess: for long-term fix we should: - decouple KV on-disk format from kernel internals (stable serialization) - make kernel adapters implement a strict packing contract - ensure migration is atomic (two-phase commit)

Mike: PR with checksum assert + test incoming. Also will add a "kernel-lock-until-terminated" config to avoid mid-request flips until migration is hardened.

Sandeep: can you add a small eval harness script to reproduce locally? Mike, Anya — add exact command so eng-runtime can run perf traces.

Anya: repro command: curl -s -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"<json-invoice-prompt>","max_tokens":64,"debug_token_trace":true}' > trace.json
Then: python3 tools/compare_traces.py --expected tests/expected/invoice.json trace.json

Mike: PR: runtime#4423 (wip) — adds kv checksum logs and unit tests. Will also add a feature-flag to disable migration.

Anya: filed eval ticket with failing example ids and attached traces: EV-8342. Adding owners: @Mike @Sandeep.

Sandeep: retrospective note — dynamic kernel switching gives good perf wins but it's high-risk when format/kv invariants are implicit. We should treat any on-the-fly state migrations as high-risk feature and gate behind stronger invariants.

Jess: agreed. Also add a step to integration test matrix that runs mixed-precision + kv-migration scenarios under small-batch/batcher merges.

Anya: thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated when PR lands and after full rollback status. :thumbsup:

InfraBot: rollback complete on 4 hosts (runtime/scheduler) at 2023-11-09T22:33:09Z — health checks OK.

Mike: running nightly eval with the rollback in place now — will post numbers in ~30m.

Sandeep: next actions captured in EV-8342 and runtime#4423. Closing triage until PR review.
